findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing the old cache status
findings.body:
On success, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (`onChanged` from the wrapper, which is often undefined). It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation in the same component does invalidate it in `onSettled`.

After a successful delete, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated: …" and the "Delete cached data" action. That stale state lasts until something else refetches the query, and `refetchOnWindowFocus` is false for this query. This contradicts the test plan's "UI updates appropriately".

Fix: invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSuccess`/`onSettled`.

findings.title: updateMany with empty data does not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
findings.body:
`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is meant to touch `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` after each cache refresh. Prisma only injects `@updatedAt` when the update has at least one field; with `data: {}` the update is a no-op. So `updatedAt` never changes, and the call is a wasted DB round trip on every webhook-driven cache refresh.

The PR description's claim that SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is updated via the webhook handler is therefore false.

Either set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly or remove the call. The PR notes the field is unused in the frontend anyway. Also note that `updateManyByCredentialId` is typed with `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` rather than `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
findings.body:
`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows for the credential and takes the max `updatedAt`, without filtering on `expiresAt >= now`. `getCachedAvailability` ignores expired rows, so a credential whose cache has fully expired is still reported as having cache data with a "Last updated" timestamp. The dropdown then shows a status for cache that is never served.

Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause.

findings.title: Plain Error used for access denial yields 500 instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN
findings.body:
When the credential does not belong to the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps a plain Error to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). As a result, authorization failures show up as server errors in monitoring and clients cannot distinguish them.

Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN), consistent with other handlers.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that nothing consumes
findings.body:
`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Nothing in this PR reads these fields; the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache.

`getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` is also exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` and has other callers. Any caller that builds the user with only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` now fails type-checking.

The change also widens the session user select (`findUnlockedUserForSession`) for no functional benefit. Revert these type and select changes unless they are needed.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hard-coded en-US locale
findings.body:
The "Last updated" timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)`, while the surrounding string is translated via `t()`. Users with other locales see US-style dates (MM/DD/YY, 12h clock) inside localized text.

Use the user's locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`), or the app's date formatting helpers, together with the user's time format preference.

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL and legacy rows get a misleading timestamp
findings.body:
The header warns that the required column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." The statement actually adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is stale and misleading.

Also, every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`. Right after deploy, the new UI reports all legacy caches as "Last updated" at migration time, regardless of when they were actually written.

findings.title: BSD-only `sed -i ''` breaks on Linux; relative ENV_FILE depends on cwd
findings.body:
`sed -i '' -E ...` is macOS/BSD syntax. With GNU sed, the empty string is parsed as the sed script and the `s|...|` expression as a filename, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails on Linux.

Separately, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 5) is resolved relative to the caller's cwd. Running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates or edits a `.env` outside the repository.

Resolve the path relative to the script directory, and use a portable in-place edit (e.g. `sed -i.bak` or a temp file).

findings.title: dev:cron relies on unpinned `npx tsx` not declared as a dependency
findings.body:
`tsx` is not listed in devDependencies, so `npx tsx` downloads whatever version is latest at run time. That requires network access and gives non-reproducible behavior. `ts-node` is still kept as a devDependency.

Add `tsx` as a pinned devDependency and invoke it directly, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache handler, cache status repository method, or dropdown
findings.body:
The PR adds a mutation that deletes data, guarded by an ownership check (`deleteCacheHandler`). It also adds `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` and new conditional rendering logic in `CredentialActionsDropdown`, but none of these have tests.

At minimum, cover these cases:
- The handler rejects credentials owned by another user.
- The handler deletes only rows for the given credential.
- The status query returns the max `updatedAt` per credential.
